about: Cross-key rules the schemas do not encode. when: all, any, not or a test of one key (set, eq, in, lt, on = a switch counts as set, effective = only the highest layer's value counts, falsy = value 0, false or empty); layer limits where the key is looked up. needsAll: the rule looks for a missing setting, so it is skipped while a settings file cannot be read. A rule without when is a static note on its keys. kind picks the title: conflict (two settings that cancel each other, Conflicting settings), hardening (advice against a default, Hardening), ignored (a setting with no effect where it is, Ignored setting) or note (Note); default, risk and fixChanges say in one sentence each what the default is, what it risks and what the fix changes for the user. {top}, {saved} and {models} in the effort texts are the top-level level, the saved one and the models that have it. Each rule cites a source url and a verbatim quote that test/settings.test.mjs finds in the pinned copy of that page (test/fixtures/settings-docs.json).

rules.message: The advisor stays off while a switch that turns feature-flag fetching off is set.
rules.fix: unset the switch, or unset advisorModel
rules.default: By default no advisor model is set, and no switch turns feature-flag fetching off.
rules.risk: With such a switch set, the advisor you chose never runs.
rules.fixChanges: Unsetting the switch turns the traffic it blocked back on; unsetting advisorModel turns the advisor off.
rules.quote: In a session where a variable that turns flag fetching off is set, such as `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`, the advisor stays off.

rules.message: The advisor ranks below the main model, so Claude Code does not attach it. Checked only for full model IDs: an alias such as opus resolves to whatever Claude Code's current default is.
rules.fix: pick an advisor that ranks at or above the main model
rules.default: By default no advisor model is set, so no advisor runs.
rules.risk: An advisor that ranks below the main model is not attached, so the setting does nothing.
rules.fixChanges: A higher-ranked advisor costs more per advisor call.
rules.quote: an advisor must rank at or above your session's main model

rules.message: Remote Control is unavailable while CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC or DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK is set, so it cannot connect at startup.
rules.fix: unset the switch, or set remoteControlAtStartup to false
rules.default: By default neither switch is set and Remote Control can connect.
rules.risk: With either switch set, Remote Control cannot connect at startup, so remoteControlAtStartup does nothing.
rules.fixChanges: Unsetting the switch turns the traffic it blocked back on; setting remoteControlAtStartup to false means you start Remote Control yourself.
rules.quote: If you set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` or `DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK`, Remote Control is unavailable.

rules.message: Remote Control stays available with only DISABLE_TELEMETRY or DO_NOT_TRACK set, unless your organization requires Trusted Devices; it needs Claude Code v2.1.283 or later.
rules.default: By default neither switch is set.
rules.risk: None: Remote Control keeps working with only these two switches set, unless your organization requires Trusted Devices.
rules.fixChanges: Nothing needs to change.
rules.quote: If you set only `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` or `DO_NOT_TRACK`, Remote Control stays available unless your organization requires

rules.message: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC stops auto-updates, so the update channel has no effect.
rules.fix: unset the switch, or unset autoUpdatesChannel
rules.default: By default the nonessential-traffic switch is unset and Claude Code updates itself on the chosen channel.
rules.risk: With the switch set, Claude Code stops updating, whatever channel you chose.
rules.fixChanges: Unsetting the switch turns auto-updates, telemetry and error reporting back on; unsetting the channel only removes a key that has no effect.
rules.quote: to disable nonessential network traffic: auto-updates, telemetry, error reporting

rules.message: Turns feature-flag fetching off: the advisor stays off, /import, /skill-doctor and idle compaction stop, Remote Control is limited, and the nonessential-traffic switch also stops auto-updates.
rules.default: By default none of these switches is set and feature flags are fetched.
rules.risk: With one set, the advisor, /import, /skill-doctor and idle compaction stop, and Remote Control is limited.
rules.fixChanges: Unsetting the switch brings those features back and sends the traffic the switch blocked.
quote: [compact a long conversation while your terminal session is idle]

rules.message: The top-level effortLevel ({top}) in the user file differs from the level {saved} saved under modelSettings for {models}: a model with a saved level uses it, and the top-level key sets only models released before Opus 5.5 that have none. Both at the same level, as BenchKeeper's setup writes, or different levels saved per model on purpose are not flagged.
rules.fix: remove effortLevel from the user file, or make it the same as the saved levels
rules.default: The top-level effortLevel is {top}; {models} have {saved} saved under modelSettings and use that.
rules.risk: Models without a saved level that came before Opus 5.5 run at {top}, the others at their saved or own default level, which may not be what you meant.
rules.fixChanges: Removing effortLevel lets older models without a saved level start at their own default; setting it to {saved} runs them at {saved}.
rules.quote: Opus 5.5 and models released after it ignore it and start at their own default until you save a level for them

rules.message: includeCoAuthoredBy is deprecated and is overruled by attribution when that sets commit or pr.
rules.fix: remove includeCoAuthoredBy
rules.default: By default includeCoAuthoredBy is true and attribution is unset.
rules.risk: With attribution set, includeCoAuthoredBy is ignored, so changing it has no effect.
rules.fixChanges: Removing includeCoAuthoredBy changes nothing in commits or pull requests: attribution decides.
rules.quote: unless `attribution` sets `commit` or `pr`

rules.message: auto and bypassPermissions in a project or local file are silently ignored; only the user file takes them.
rules.fix: remove the key from the project or local file, or set it in the user file
rules.default: By default permissions.defaultMode is unset.
rules.risk: auto or bypassPermissions in a project or local file is ignored, so sessions start in another mode than you expect.
rules.fixChanges: Moving the key to the user file makes the mode apply to every project.
rules.quote: `auto` and `bypassPermissions` don't take effect from project or local settings

rules.message: Transcripts older than this many days are deleted without a message; the Sessions board reads them, so a value below 30 shortens its history.
rules.fix: raise cleanupPeriodDays to 30 or more, or keep it on purpose
rules.default: By default Claude Code keeps transcripts for 30 days.
rules.risk: A shorter period deletes transcripts sooner, and the Sessions board loses that history.
rules.fixChanges: A longer period keeps more transcripts on disk.
rules.quote: The sweep deletes transcripts without showing a message

rules.message: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB is off: Bash commands, hooks and stdio MCP servers inherit the whole environment, provider and cloud tokens included.
rules.fix: set env.CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB to 1 in the user settings, unless a subprocess needs a variable it removes
rules.default: By default the scrub is off and every subprocess inherits the whole environment.
rules.risk: A Bash command, hook or MCP server that is tricked or malicious can read your provider and cloud tokens.
rules.fixChanges: With the scrub on, a tool that reads a credential from the environment stops working until you pass that variable another way.
rules.quote: Set to `1` to strip credentials from the environments of the subprocesses Claude Code starts

rules.message: No Read deny rule covers every one of the .ssh, .aws and .config/gh folders, so Claude's file tools can read those credential files.
rules.fix: add Read(//**/.ssh/**), Read(//**/.aws/**) and Read(//**/.config/gh/**) to permissions.deny in the user settings; a script that opens the files itself is still not covered
rules.default: By default there are no deny rules, so Claude can read any file you can.
rules.risk: A prompt injection can make Claude read your SSH keys, cloud credentials or GitHub token.
rules.fixChanges: With the deny rules, Claude can no longer read those folders, also when you ask it to.
quote: add a `Read` deny rule for its path
They don't apply to a command that reads files without naming them

rules.message: sandbox.enabled is off, or the managed sandbox.enabledPlatforms leaves this platform out: Bash commands run with your full rights, so a prompt injection that reaches a shell can write anywhere you can and send data to any host.
rules.fix: set sandbox.enabled to true (benchkeeper settings set sandbox.enabled true), in the user settings or per project; it covers shell commands only; if a managed sandbox.enabledPlatforms list leaves this platform out, only the managed settings can change that: ask your administrator to add it
rules.default: By default the sandbox is off and Bash commands run with your full rights.
rules.risk: A prompt injection that reaches a shell can write anywhere you can and send data to any host.
rules.fixChanges: With the sandbox on, commands that write outside the project or reach hosts not on the list are blocked or ask first.
rules.quote: The sandbox runs on macOS, Linux, and WSL2.

rules.message: sandbox.failIfUnavailable is not true while sandbox.enabled is on: when the sandbox cannot start (a missing program, an unsupported platform) Claude Code runs commands without it.
rules.fix: set sandbox.failIfUnavailable to true (benchkeeper settings set sandbox.failIfUnavailable true)
rules.default: By default failIfUnavailable is false, so commands run unsandboxed when the sandbox cannot start.
rules.risk: A missing program or an unsupported platform silently turns the sandbox off.
rules.fixChanges: With it true, Claude Code does not start when the sandbox cannot start.
rules.quote: Claude Code runs commands without sandboxing

rules.message: sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands is not false: Claude may retry a command that the sandbox blocked outside the sandbox.
rules.fix: set sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands to false (benchkeeper settings set sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands false)
rules.default: By default allowUnsandboxedCommands is true, so a command the sandbox blocked may be retried outside it.
rules.risk: A retried command runs with your full rights, past the sandbox.
rules.fixChanges: With it false, a command the sandbox blocks stays blocked until you allow it in the sandbox settings.
rules.quote: disable the unsandboxed retry by setting

rules.message: bubblewrap (bwrap) is not on the PATH while sandbox.enabled is on, so the sandbox cannot start on Linux and WSL2.
rules.fix: install bubblewrap (Debian, Ubuntu, WSL2: apt install bubblewrap socat; Fedora: dnf install bubblewrap socat), or set sandbox.bwrapPath to its absolute path in the managed settings
rules.default: By default the sandbox is off and needs no extra program.
rules.risk: With the sandbox on and bubblewrap missing, the sandbox cannot start on Linux and WSL2.
rules.fixChanges: Installing bubblewrap lets the sandbox start; nothing else changes.
rules.quote: the sandbox relies on `bubblewrap` and `socat`

rules.message: socat is not on the PATH while sandbox.enabled is on, so the sandbox cannot start on Linux and WSL2.
rules.fix: install socat (Debian, Ubuntu, WSL2: apt install bubblewrap socat; Fedora: dnf install bubblewrap socat), or set sandbox.socatPath to its absolute path in the managed settings
rules.default: By default the sandbox is off and needs no extra program.
rules.risk: With the sandbox on and socat missing, the sandbox cannot start on Linux and WSL2.
rules.fixChanges: Installing socat lets the sandbox start; nothing else changes.
rules.quote: the sandbox relies on `bubblewrap` and `socat`

rules.message: sandbox.network.allowedDomains is empty: a command that reaches a new host can prompt for approval or be blocked, depending on the permission mode and the strictAllowlist and allowManagedDomainsOnly settings. Listing the hosts you expect (your package registry, your git host) avoids those prompts and blocks; BenchKeeper never writes the list, it is your choice.
rules.fix: add hosts to sandbox.network.allowedDomains, or leave it empty and answer any prompts
rules.default: By default the list of allowed hosts is empty.
rules.risk: Each new host a command reaches asks for approval or is blocked, which interrupts work.
rules.fixChanges: Listing hosts lets commands reach them without asking, so pick only hosts you trust.
rules.quote: your allowed domains start empty

rules.message: Claude Code's sandbox is unsupported on native Windows: commands run unsandboxed whatever sandbox.enabled says, and Claude Code exits at startup when sandbox.failIfUnavailable is true, unless a managed sandbox.enabledPlatforms list leaves Windows out. Run Claude Code inside WSL2 to use the sandbox.
rules.default: By default the sandbox is off.
rules.risk: On native Windows commands always run unsandboxed, and failIfUnavailable true stops Claude Code at startup.
rules.fixChanges: Running Claude Code inside WSL2 makes the sandbox available.
quote: On native Windows, Claude Code runs commands unsandboxed.
with `failIfUnavailable` set, Claude Code exits at startup on those machines

rules.message: {key} counts as set even with 0 or false.
rules.fix: remove {key}; the editor writes 1 or removes the key
rules.default: By default the switch is unset.
rules.risk: A value of 0 or false still turns the switch on, the opposite of what it reads like.
rules.fixChanges: Removing the key turns the switch off.
quote: **Setting it to `0` or `false` still opts out**
**Setting it to `0` or `false` still disables this traffic**

rules.message: OpenTelemetry export variables in a project or local env block are ignored; set them in the user settings, the shell or managed settings.
rules.fix: move the variable to the user file
rules.default: By default no OpenTelemetry variable is set.
rules.risk: Set in a project or local file, the variables are ignored and nothing is exported.
rules.fixChanges: Moving them to the user file exports telemetry from every project.
rules.quote: Ignored in [project and local settings]

rules.message: {key}: {note}
rules.fix: remove {key} from the file
rules.default: By default the key is unset.
rules.risk: A deprecated or removed key does nothing, so the behavior you set it for does not happen.
rules.fixChanges: Removing the key changes nothing, since Claude Code already ignores it.

rules.message: The classifier does not read autoMode from a project or local file, so its rules have no effect there; only the user file (or managed settings) takes it.
rules.fix: move autoMode to the user file
rules.default: By default autoMode is unset and the built-in classifier rules apply.
rules.risk: In a project or local file the rules are ignored, so the classifier decides without them.
rules.fixChanges: Moving autoMode to the user file makes the rules apply to every project.
rules.quote: The classifier doesn't read `autoMode` from project settings in `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json`.

rules.message: The docs say false also disables custom OTLP metrics exporters; the schema at rust-v0.164.0 says they stay enabled and are controlled by otel.metrics_exporter. Set that key to "none" to be sure.
rules.default: By default analytics follows the client default.
rules.risk: The docs and the schema disagree on whether analytics.enabled false also stops custom metrics export.
rules.fixChanges: Setting otel.metrics_exporter to none stops metrics export for certain.
rules.quote: false also disables custom OTLP metrics exporters

rules.message: A project-local .codex/config.toml cannot set notify or otel (they are ignored there), and it loads only for trusted projects.
rules.fix: move the key to the user config
rules.default: By default notify and otel are unset.
rules.risk: Set in a project config, they are ignored, so no notification or telemetry happens.
rules.fixChanges: Moving them to the user config applies them to every project.
rules.quote: notify , profile , profiles , experimental_realtime_ws_base_url , and otel when they appear in a project-local .codex/config.toml

rules.message: default_permissions is not combined with sandbox_mode.
rules.fix: keep one of them
rules.default: By default neither key is set.
rules.risk: Both together are not supported, so the permissions you get may not be the ones you meant.
rules.fixChanges: Keeping one of them decides the permissions alone.
rules.quote: Don't combine with sandbox_mode or [sandbox_workspace_write]

rules.message: approval_policy never with sandbox_mode danger-full-access runs every command without a prompt and without a sandbox.
rules.fix: use on-request with workspace-write
rules.default: By default neither key is set to these values.
rules.risk: Every command runs without a prompt and without a sandbox, so a prompt injection can do anything you can.
rules.fixChanges: With on-request and workspace-write, commands outside the workspace ask first.
rules.quote: on-request | never |

rules.message: sandbox_mode is danger-full-access: commands run without a sandbox, with full file and network access.
rules.fix: use workspace-write (benchkeeper settings set sandbox_mode workspace-write --agent codex), or read-only
rules.default: By default sandbox_mode is unset.
rules.risk: Commands run without a sandbox, with full file and network access.
rules.fixChanges: With workspace-write, commands that write outside the workspace or use the network ask first or are blocked.
rules.quote: Sandbox policy for filesystem and network access during command execution.

rules.message: Folders in [projects."<path>"] that no longer exist (worktrees pile up there) are listed with a remove action; nothing is removed on its own.
rules.default: By default the trust list holds every folder you trusted.
rules.risk: Entries for folders that are gone pile up; they do nothing else.
rules.fixChanges: Removing an entry changes nothing for existing folders.
rules.quote: projects.<path>.trust_level
